name: Structure Check
description: Runs every structural rule on each change quickly enough that nobody skips it, reports each finding by rule and path with its next action, and keeps rule exceptions honest by reporting those that no longer apply. The rules are numbered modules written to one interface, each with the one-line statement of what it checks.
purpose: Run every structural rule on each change and report each finding by rule and path with its next action, quickly enough that nobody skips it.
approach: Run every enabled rule against the tree, report findings by rule id and path with the next action, and flag any accepted exception that no longer applies. A rule is a numbered module written to one interface, shipped with the library and extended by plugins.
out_of_scope: Deciding whether a rule earns its place; judging quality beyond the rules.
milestones: 1. Violation detection: every injected violation is reported by the right rule and path. [met: 2026-10-26] 2. Check dependability: a clean tree is never flagged and an exception that no longer applies is always reported, and all mutation cases pass. [met: 2026-10-26]
knowledge: Architecture tests and linters (import-linter, ArchUnit); plugin systems; the repository's numbered rules (esoi rules); the leaderboard (reused, not copied).
measures_of_success: Every injected violation is reported by the right rule and path, a clean tree is never flagged, an exception that no longer applies is reported, and the run is fast enough that nobody skips it. Standing conditions: Any rule written to the rule interface runs and reports by rule and path; a repository can disable a rule or add its own; each rule catches a mistake that has happened.
parameters: Strict mode; the rule ids to disable; the plugins to load; per-rule settings such as the module size ceiling and the layers.
inputs: The repository, the registry, the results log, the waivers, the configuration.
outputs: A list of violations, each led by its rule id, and an exit code.
effects: Blocks a commit or a test run that breaks a rule.
usage_notes: Keep the runner free of any one rule: a new rule is a rule group written to the interface, never an edit to the runner. Add a rule when a mistake has happened twice; whether a rule stays is the business of the structure budget.
change_driver: the system's own data model or code
